title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
abstract: We show that the Werner state $ρ= (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $ρ$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

bite.hook: Proved that a specific Werner state in C^8 tensor C^8 is bound entangled with a negative partial transpose.
tldr: Analyzed a specific Werner state defined on an 8-by-8 complex vector space.
Tested its entanglement properties using partial transpose and local operations with classical communication (LOCC).
Found it is bound entangled with a negative partial transpose, proving distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.
bite.whyItMatters: This resolves fundamental mathematical questions about the nature of quantum entanglement, showing that some types of locked quantum correlations cannot be neatly broken down or added together.
bite.eli5: Think of quantum entanglement like locked puzzle boxes. The author found a specific box that is glued shut in such a weird way that you can prove the pieces are linked, but you can never actually pull a clean, usable piece out of it.
